items.stem: Using Roediger and Karpicke (2006) as supporting evidence, explain retrieval practice as a learning strategy.
items.answer: Roediger and Karpicke (2006). Aim: to investigate whether testing improves long-term retention of prose more than restudying. Method: Students read short prose passages and then either studied them repeatedly (SSSS), studied three times and were tested once (SSST), or studied once and were tested three times (STTT); recall was tested after 5 minutes or 1 week. Findings: after 5 minutes repeated study was slightly better, but after one week the STTT group recalled about 61% compared with about 40% for SSSS Link: retrieval practice as a learning strategy.

items.stem: With reference to Kruger and Dunning (1999), explain how research has investigated limits of metacognitive monitoring.
items.answer: Kruger and Dunning (1999). Aim: to investigate whether people with low competence lack the metacognitive skill to recognise it. Method: Cornell students completed tests of humour, logical reasoning and grammar, then estimated their ability and test score relative to peers. Findings: participants in the bottom quartile greatly overestimated their performance (estimating around the 62nd percentile when they were at about the 12th) Link: limits of metacognitive monitoring.

items.stem: Describe the study by Ophir, Nass and Wagner (2009) and explain what it shows about the effects of media multitasking on attention.
items.answer: Ophir, Nass and Wagner (2009). Aim: to compare the cognitive control of heavy and light media multitaskers. Method: Stanford students were classified as heavy or light media multitaskers using a questionnaire, then completed tasks measuring filtering of distractors, working memory and task switching. Findings: heavy multitaskers were more affected by irrelevant stimuli and were slower to switch tasks than light multitaskers Link: the effects of media multitasking on attention.

items.stem: With reference to MTA Cooperative Group (1999), explain how research has investigated treatment of ADHD.
items.answer: MTA Cooperative Group (1999). Aim: to compare the long-term effectiveness of medication, behavioural treatment, their combination and community care for ADHD. Method: 579 children aged 7-9 with ADHD were randomly assigned to 14 months of medication management, intensive behavioural treatment, combined treatment or standard community care at six sites. Findings: carefully managed medication and combined treatment reduced core ADHD symptoms more than behavioural treatment or community care; combined treatment had added benefits for some outcomes Link: treatment of ADHD.

items.stem: "Neurodevelopmental differences such as ADHD are best understood as biological disorders." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Biological factors are important, but outcomes depend heavily on environment and support; a biopsychosocial view is most useful.

items.answer: Massed practice concentrates study into one long session (cramming), producing good short-term but poor long-term retention; spaced practice distributes study across sessions, giving better long-term retention.
